name: Oromo
variant: Western-Central Oromo (Wollega and Shewa usage, the standard of media and schools in Oromia) in Qubee Latin script
script: Latin (Qubee) with c, q, x and ph for ejectives, ch, dh, ny, sh as digraphs, ' (hudhaa) for the glottal stop, and doubled letters for long vowels and long consonants; left to right
basis: Peace Corps Ethiopia, Oromo for Beginners (Dejenie Leta, 1975, Western Oromo of Wollega, Illubabor and Kaffa): greetings, pronouns, possessive endings, numbers, food and drink, imperatives, days, months and time, family, transport, adjectives and colours, prepositions, directions, the market, states of being, with 'to be' and verb conjugation in the appendix
src: Peace Corps, Oromo for Beginners by Dejenie Leta (Awassa, 1975; ERIC ED226615), table of contents and grammatical appendix headings, opened as a scanned PDF through a web reader
note: The source is from 1975, before Qubee was adopted, and the scan is damaged, so no Oromo spelling was taken from it: every Oromo form in the titles is in modern Qubee from my own knowledge. The variety follows the source (Western, Wollega), which is close to the Central standard used in schools and media. The topic order (greetings, pronouns, possessives, numbers, food, commands, days and time, family, transport, adjectives and colours, postpositions, directions, the market) follows the source loosely. The source teaches grammar mostly in an appendix, so the grammar lessons (dha and miti, the subject ending -n / -ni, present, negative and past verb forms, jira, question words) and their order are common course practice and my own judgment. I moved food, time and commands after the first verb lessons so they can use verbs. The split into 23 lessons is mine.
hardest: Ejective sounds written c, q, x and ph, and the glottal stop written '
Long vowels and long consonants that change meaning, written doubled (lafa / laafaa)
Verb-final word order, with verb endings for person and gender (ni deema, ni deemti)
The subject form of nouns: maqaa becomes maqaan, nama becomes namni

items: Qubee: the alphabet, with c, q, x and ph for ejectives and ch, dh, ny, sh
Long vowels, double consonants and the glottal stop: lafa / laafaa, taa'i
Greetings: Akkam?, Nagaa, Akkam bulte?, Galatoomi, Nagaatti
Pronouns: ani, ati, inni, isheen, nuti, isin, isaan
Introducing yourself: Maqaan koo … dha, Maqaan kee eenyu?, Eessaa dhufte?
'To be' with dha, and miti: Ani barsiisaa dha, Ani barsiisaa miti
The subject ending -n / -ni: maqaa → maqaan, nama → namni
Possessives: koo, kee, isaa, ishee (maqaa koo, mana kee)
Question words: maal, eenyu, eessa, yoom, meeqa, akkam
Numbers: tokko, lama, sadii … kudhan, digdama, dhibba
Present tense: nan deema, ni deemta, ni deema, ni deemti
Past tense: deeme, deemte, and the negative hin deemne
Commands: kottu, taa'i, deemi, and the plural kottaa
Where things are: keessa, irra, jala, -tti, and jira (there is)
Food and drink: buddeena, bishaan, aannan, buna
Days and time: Wiixata, Kibxata, Roobii; Sa'aatii meeqa?
Adjectives after the noun: mana guddaa, xiqqaa, gaarii; colours diimaa, adii, gurraacha
At the market: Gatiin isaa meeqa?, qarshii
Directions and transport: mirga, bitaa, kallattiin; konkolaataa
How you feel: hunger, thirst, tiredness and health
